text:
Dmitri Kuznetsov: Heads up — we saw a ~27% increase in GPU preemptions in us-west1 over the last 2h, and it translated to ~12% tail latency spikes for our batch inference lanes. Thinking we should iterate on autoscaler behavior for spot-backed pools: small hot reserve per-region, a soft "hedge" lane (cheap spot but capped), and longer-cooldown cold starters. Looking for concrete thresholds/cooldowns. cc @Priya @Sam :thinking:

Priya Raman: Definitely noticed the blips. Two quick numbers: 1) cost for keeping a 5% hot reserve across fleets ≈ +3.5% monthly, 2) that buys ~45s median recovery vs cold start. My gut: reserve_fraction 0.03-0.07 depending on region load variance. Also +1 for a separate eviction buffer metric to avoid flapping. :+1:

Sam Lee: Agree. Also want to avoid simultaneous scale-ups across models (fan-out). Proposal: stagger canary scale-outs using model-group tags and add a small randomized jitter to scale decisions. Example config:
```yaml
autoscaler:
  min_replicas: 2
  max_replicas: 200
  reserve_fraction: 0.05       # hot pool per region
  hedge_lane:
    enabled: true
    max_replicas: 0.2          # fraction of max for soft-spot lane
    eviction_buffer_secs: 120  # buffer to tolerate short preemptions
  scale_out_threshold_qps: 1200
  scale_in_threshold_qps: 300
  surge_capacity: 0.15        # allow temporary overshoot of replicas
  cool_down_seconds:
    scale_out: 60
    scale_in: 900
  preemption_window_secs: 300
  jitter_ms: 4000
```

Marta Alvarez: Two product constraints to consider: 1) models with large KV caches (chat) suffer more from cold starts — give them a higher reserve_fraction or pin to dedicated lanes; 2) batch small-sequence models tolerate longer cooldowns. Suggest per-model-profile overrides: reserve_fraction heavy-cache=0.12, small-batch=0.02. Also add a prompt to evict KV cache only after X successful warm requests. :eyes:

Dmitri Kuznetsov: Good points. On surge controls — we should limit cross-region failover to avoid blowing commit budgets. Maybe a global cap on cross-region hedging (e.g., 10% of global capacity) and per-region soft cap. Thoughts?

Priya Raman: 👍 global cap helps. Also recommend a rolling eviction-aware drain: when we detect >threshold preemptions, reduce scale_out aggressiveness for 5m and grow reserve by +2% for the same window. That buys headroom without huge cost.

autoscale-bot: [ALERT] preemption-spike detected in us-west1; 18 preemptions in 15m. Current reserve_fraction=0.03; estimated headroom exhaustion in 8m.

Sam Lee: Let's add an adaptive reserve bump rule: if preemption_rate > X then reserve_fraction += min(0.05, 2 * measured_spike). Also reduce batch window batching for the duration so we don't overload in-flight KV warms. We can implement as a policy in the autoscaler controller.

Marta Alvarez: For experiments, can we A/B the config by model-group? Group A: reserve_fraction fixed at 5%, Group B: adaptive bump. Measure median recovery time and cost delta for 24h. If recovery_time drops >30% with <6% cost increase, promote.

Dmitri Kuznetsov: Plan: I'll prototype the controller change and a canary in us-west1 for a subset of batch models. Sam, can you add the YAML variant as a rollout patch? Priya/Marta — will you own the canary monitoring and validation criteria? :rocket:

Priya Raman: I can own monitoring. I'll add dashboards: reserve fraction, preemption rate, median recovery time, tail p95/p99 latency, and cost burn. Will alert if cost delta >6% or recovery_time not improving.

Sam Lee: Will add patch. Adding jitter and stagger tags to rollout plan.

Marta Alvarez: I'll prepare the model-group split and the eval harness (synthetic preemption injection + traffic replay).

Dmitri Kuznetsov: Cool. Let's reconvene after a 24h canary. Thanks all. :+1:
